newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends lower in technical pullback.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends lower in technical pullback.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended lower Thursday in a technical pullback that followed morning weakness in natural gas futures, industry sources said.
"Technically, (electricity) was overbought, these are good values," one futures broker said of Thursday's settles.
Front month electricity futures hit all time highs in morning trade, following rising gas futures, but when gas tumbled electricity was right behind.
NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures rallied at the end of the day to hit an all-time high of $4.00 per million British thermal units, but electricity failed to follow.
"Overall gas was beginning to show the early signs of some weakness, and that did reflect on electricity," the broker said.
Electricity futures could continue to fall on Friday, which is expiry day for December PV and COB, the sources said.
December California Oregon Border (COB) finished down $1.49 per megawatt hour (MWh) at $27.91 after hitting an all time contract high of $32.00 and trading as low as $27.00
January COB finished down $1.12 at $24.63 after trading at a new contract high of $26.00 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds closed down between 30 to 97 cents.
December Palo Verde (PV) ended down $1.49 at $27.91 after hitting an all time contract high of $32.00 and trading as low as $27.00 per MWh.
January PV ended down $1.18 at $24.00 after hitting a new contract high of $26.00 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds settled down between 25 cents and $1.65.
NYMEX said a total of 382 COB and 258 PV contracts traded.
